_comment: WHO-IRIS, declared as an INSTANTIATED harness. Owner, 2026-09-21, looking at the home page: 'why dont i see who-iris as a harness on LHS on home navbar?' It WAS on the navbar — filed under `Dependencies`, inside a `<details>` that ships closed, because `harness-tiles.ts` computes `instantiated` from whether the instantiation root carries `<name>.config.json` and this file did not exist. That is the rule the owner set ('scan the root of the repo, look for <harness>.config.json as named instances'), so the rule was right and the FACT was wrong: this repository does instantiate who-iris — it holds the catalogue, generates and gates the replica pages, and publishes them at /who-iris/. The fix is therefore this declaration rather than an edit to the template, and nothing in `nav_footer_custom.html` changes: who-iris moves into the open `Harnesses` group because the generated data now says it belongs there. Keeping the display and the fact in one answer is the whole point — the alternative, opening the Dependencies group, would have shown who-iris while still recording it as something this repo merely depends on.
_contentType_comment: `document`, not `paper`. who-iris holds structured prose — the ingested IRIS replica, the DSpace item records, the style guide's page sections — and no Lean and no TeX. Declaring `paper` would run the paper adapter's LaTeX-shaped QA axes over content that never reaches pdflatex, which is the `critical`-on-prose failure `cat-harness.config.json` records in its own comment.
